lawyer:
Tufailur Rahman along with Sufiya Ahmed, Advocates Taimur Reza (Hasan), Advocate — For the Petitioners. 
Ozair Farook with SK Md Morshed, Advocates —For the Opposite Party.
parties:
Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation (BJMC) and others ----- Petitioners
Vs. 
SM Fakhrul Islam Chowdhury ----- Opposite-Party
full_judgment:
The sole opposite party as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 292 of 2000 before the Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Dhaka, praying for a decree for declaration that the order of dismissal from service dated 15-1-1991 is illegal, void and not binding upon him. In the suit it was stated that the plaintiff was serving under the defendant with the entire satisfaction to the Corporation. All on a sudden, the defendant-petitioners suspended the plaintiff vide order No. 516/1467 dated 29-9-1989 on the ground that a first information report was lodged against him. Following the suspension, a charge-sheet was issued on 6-3-1990, the plaintiff replied to the same on 14-3-1990, an inquiry was held and after inquiry an inquiry report was submitted on 6-6-1990. Thereafter, the second show cause notice was issued on 19-9-1990 of which the plaintiff replied to the same on 30-9-90. While the position was such, after a trial in the criminal case arising out of the aforesaid first information report the plaintiff was acquitted on 8-12-1990 of the charges brought against him. In the premises, the plaintiff submitted an application on 14-1-1991 to the defendant for his reinstatement in his service. The defendant-petitioner instead of allowing him to join in the service, dismissed him from service vide order dated 15-1-1991. On 26-1-1991, the plaintiff filed an application for reviewing the dismissal order dated 15-1-1999 and without having any remedy again filed an application before the Chairman BJMC for his re-instatement in service and then legal notice through lawyer and having no reply or result from the defendants, was constrained to file the present suit. 

 3. The petitioners as defendants, contested the suit by filing written statement. Their case was that a 3-member committee was formed to investigate into the allegation against the plaintiff and after a proper departmental proceedings and observing all formalities he was dismissed from the service in accordance with the service regulation and law. 

 6. Mr. Tufailur Rahman assisted by Ms Sufiya Ahmed, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the defendants petitioners submits that the judgment and decree of the appellate Court is based upon misconception of law and facts and the appellate Court below failed to consider the facts and circumstances of the case. The plaintiff having been found guilty in the departmental proceeding was dismissed from service in accordance with service regulation and, as such, the appellate Court below committed an error of law apparent on the face of the record in setting aside the decree. He further submits that though the plaintiff was acquitted of criminal charges even then, there is no bar from departmental proceeding, independent of each other and hence the judgment and decree of the appellate Court below is liable to be set aside. The alleged act of theft and misconduct having been established in the departmental proceeding yet the appellate Court below held that the order of dismissal is without lawful authority and thence the judgment and decree of the appellate Court is liable to be set aside. He finally submits that the plaintiff was dismissed from service upon complying with all legal formalities and the appellate Court was wrong in interfering with the departmental proceeding and the action of the defendants. 

 7. Mr. Ozair Farook assisted by Mr. Sk Md Morshed, the learned Advocates appearing on behalf of the opposite party, submits that the defendants dismissed the plaintiff without giving any opportunity of being heard and violated the principles of natural justice. The defendants without following the provisions of Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation Employees Service Regulation, 1990 concluded the departmental proceeding and the trial Court upon a misconception of law and misreading of the evidence and materials on record and without considering the legal aspect of the case dismissed the suit. The appellate Court, on appeal by the plaintiff as final Court of fact, reversed the judgment of the trial Court and decreed the suit on proper assessment and appreciation of the evidence on record and committed no error of law and, as such, the impugned judgment is not liable to be interfered with by this Court. 

 12. I have considered the entire facts and circumstances and I am of the view that the trial Court dismissed the suit completely upon misconception of relevant law and misreading of evidence and materials on record and without considering the legal aspect of the case. The appellate Court as the final Court of fact reversed the judgment of the trial Court and decreed the suit on a proper assessment of evidence on record. Since the findings of the appellate Court do not suffer from any legal infirmity nor effects merit of the case concluded by finding of facts and it needs no interference of this Court under section 115 of the Code of Civil Procedure. 

 13. In the instant case from the judgment of the appellate Court it is found that the appellate Court carefully considered the material facts, circumstances and evidence on record and both the oral and documentary evidence including the fact that' the departmental proceeding, was concluded by the corporation violating Rule 43(8) of the Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation Service Regulations. The appellate Court also considered the principles laid down in the case of Bangladesh Oil, Gas and Mineral Corporation (Petro Bangla) and another vs Bazlul Karim reported in 1996 DLR (AD) 25 and the case of Malik Afzal Hossain vs Bangladesh Jute Mills Corporation and others reported in 1998 BLD 686 and I am of the view that these decisions are considered in accordance with the law. In view of the above findings, there is nothing to interfere with the impugned judgment.
